# IoT Atlas

> Independent IoT decision platform covering devices, protocols, apps, cloud platforms and marketplace rankings across English, Spanish and French markets.

## What this site is

- A structured IoT catalogue plus editorial decision tools, not a shop and not a review farm.
- Every record links to an official source. Marketplace ranks, prices and ASINs are prototype placeholders until a licensed Amazon data source is connected.
- Editorial scores are opinionated, documented and not financial or investment advice.

## Coverage

- 30 IoT category hubs
- 290 brands, including 268 non-cloud brands
- 998 mobile app records with Google Play and App Store links, across 25 app categories
- App categories: AI Toys & Education, Access Control, Air & Water, Audio & Headphones, Dash Cams, Drones, EV Charging, Electrical, Energy & Solar, Health, Health & Home, Infrared & Remotes, Label Printers, Lighting, Pet Tech, Projectors, Robot Vacuums, Security, Smart Garden, Smart Home, Smart Locks, TV & Streaming, Tracking, Trail Cameras, Wearables
- 29 cloud, IoT and connectivity platforms
- 49 structured comparisons scored across decision factors
- 96 ranked marketplace products across 23 categories
- 47 compatibility guides, 32 product model and manual records, 40 troubleshooting guides and 44 certification references
- 61 protocols, 47 standards, 42 guides, 33 concepts

## Pre-rendered entity pages

- Every brand, app, platform, protocol, comparison, category, model, compatibility guide, troubleshooting guide and certification has its own static page.
- Brand: https://hi-spark.net/brand/<slug>.html   App: https://hi-spark.net/app/<slug>.html
- Platform: https://hi-spark.net/cloud/<slug>.html   Protocol: https://hi-spark.net/protocol/<slug>.html
- Comparison: https://hi-spark.net/compare/<slug>.html   Category: https://hi-spark.net/category/<slug>.html
- Compatibility: https://hi-spark.net/compatibility/<slug>.html   Model: https://hi-spark.net/model/<slug>.html
- Troubleshooting: https://hi-spark.net/troubleshooting/<slug>.html   Certification: https://hi-spark.net/certification/<slug>.html
- Full index: https://hi-spark.net/sitemap-entities.xml

## Answer formats and citation

- Compatibility, model, troubleshooting and certification pages each open with a Quick answer paragraph, a key-facts grid and a copy-ready citation line.
- Citation format: IoT Atlas. "<page title>". https://hi-spark.net/<path>. Last verified <YYYY-MM-DD>.
- Every record carries a last-verified date and links to the official source, so a statement can be traced back to the issuer before it is used in a compliance decision.
- Certification records state what a scheme covers and what it does not cover, which keeps an answer scoped to the right market and product type.
- Machine-readable data lives in /assets/*.js and the full static index is https://hi-spark.net/sitemap-entities.xml.

## Protocols covered

- Wi-Fi (Wireless LAN): High-bandwidth wireless networking for cameras, hubs, appliances and home devices.
- Bluetooth LE (Short-range): Low-energy pairing and control for wearables, locks, sensors and configuration.
- Zigbee (Mesh): Low-power mesh networking widely used in sensors, lighting, locks and smart-home hubs.
- Thread (IPv6 mesh): Low-power IPv6 mesh designed for Matter, smart-home devices and border routers.
- Matter (Application standard): Cross-ecosystem application layer for smart-home devices across Wi-Fi, Ethernet and Thread.
- Z-Wave (Mesh): Sub-GHz mesh ecosystem common in security, locks, lighting and hubs.
- MQTT (IoT messaging): Publish-subscribe messaging protocol designed for constrained devices and unreliable networks.
- HTTPS & REST (Application / API): Secure request-response APIs used by cloud platforms, mobile apps and device management tools.
- CoAP (Constrained web): UDP-based protocol for constrained IoT devices and low-bandwidth networks.
- AMQP (Enterprise messaging): Message-oriented protocol used by enterprise IoT platforms and cloud integrations.
- LoRaWAN (LPWAN): Long-range, low-power wide-area networking for sensors, agriculture and utility metering.
- NB-IoT (Cellular LPWAN): Narrowband cellular service for low-power, low-data sensors and meters.
- LTE-M (Cellular LPWAN): LTE-based low-power cellular connectivity with better mobility and latency than NB-IoT.
- 4G LTE (Cellular broadband): Cellular broadband for cameras, routers, hotspots and remote sites.
- 5G (Cellular broadband): High-throughput, low-latency cellular connectivity for gateways, video and industrial deployments.
- eSIM (SIM technology): Embedded, remotely provisioned SIM profile for cellular devices and global fleets.
- GNSS (Positioning): Satellite positioning using GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou and related constellations.
- Ultra-Wideband (Wireless / ranging): Centimetre-accurate ranging for secure access and precise indoor location.
- NFC (Short-range): Very short-range tap, pairing and payment technology.
- RFID (Identification): Radio-frequency identification for inventory, access and asset identification.
- Modbus (Industrial / fieldbus): Decades-old industrial protocol, still the default for PLCs, meters and inverters.
- OPC UA (Industrial interoperability): Secure industrial communication standard for machines, PLCs and industrial software.
- RS-485 (Industrial / physical layer): Differential serial physical layer used by Modbus RTU, BACnet MS/TP and many sensors.
- Ethernet (Wired LAN): Reliable wired networking for NVRs, gateways, industrial devices and fixed infrastructure.
- PoE (Power over Ethernet): Combines data and power on Ethernet cabling for cameras, access points and IoT endpoints.
- Wi-Fi HaLow (Long-range Wi-Fi): Sub-GHz Wi-Fi standard for longer-range, lower-power IoT devices.
- Wi-Fi 6E / 7 (High-performance Wi-Fi): Modern Wi-Fi generations with higher throughput, lower latency and 6 GHz support.
- Bluetooth Mesh (Mesh / BLE): Many-to-many BLE mesh aimed at commercial lighting and building control.
- IPv6 (Network layer): Modern internet addressing and routing foundation for scalable IoT networks.
- Digital Twin (Data model): Virtual representation of a physical device, asset or process for monitoring and simulation.
- Matter over Wi-Fi (Application / IP): Matter application layer carried over Wi-Fi for mains-powered devices.
- Thread 1.4 (Mesh / IPv6): Latest Thread release adding better border router management, Thread over Infrastructure and improved diagnostics.
- Wi-SUN (Mesh / LPWAN): IEEE 802.15.4g based field area network for large outdoor smart-city and utility meshes.
- Zigbee Green Power (Mesh / energy harvesting): Energy-harvesting profile that lets batteryless switches and sensors join a Zigbee network.
- Bluetooth Channel Sounding (Wireless / ranging): Precise distance measurement over BLE for secure access and asset tracking.
- 5G RedCap (Cellular / 5G): Reduced-capability 5G for wearables, industrial sensors and cameras that do not need full eMBB.
- Satellite NTN IoT (Satellite / non-terrestrial): Direct-to-satellite connectivity for devices outside terrestrial coverage.
- Sigfox / 0G (LPWAN / unlicensed): Ultra-narrowband, very low data rate network for simple telemetry.
- mioty (LPWAN / telegram splitting): ETSI-standardised LPWAN using telegram splitting for high reliability in dense networks.
- Wireless M-Bus (Metering / sub-GHz): European standard for wireless utility metering in the 868 MHz band.
- Z-Wave Long Range (Mesh / sub-GHz): Z-Wave LR removes repeater limits and extends range for large installations.
- CAN bus (Industrial / vehicle): Robust vehicle and machine bus, now paired with IoT gateways for telematics.
- LoRa point-to-point (LPWAN / physical): Raw LoRa modulation without LoRaWAN, used for simple private links.
- KNX (Building automation): Long-established building automation standard for lighting, HVAC and blinds.
- DALI-2 (Lighting control): Digital addressable lighting interface with certified control gear and sensors.
- Ethernet TSN (Industrial / deterministic): Time-Sensitive Networking adds determinism and time sync to standard Ethernet.
- MQTT-SN (Messaging / constrained): MQTT for Sensor Networks, adapted for very constrained devices and non-TCP links.
- AirPrint (Printing / IP): Apple driverless printing over the local network.
- IPP (Printing / IP): Internet Printing Protocol, the standard behind driverless and cloud printing.
- ESC/POS (Printing / receipt): Epson command set that became the de facto standard for receipt and label printers.
- ZPL (Printing / label): Zebra Programming Language used to compose barcode and RFID labels.
- Bluetooth A2DP (Audio / Bluetooth): Profile that carries stereo audio to headphones and speakers.
- Bluetooth LE Audio (Audio / Bluetooth): Next-generation Bluetooth audio with LC3 codec, multi-stream and broadcast.
- AirPlay 2 (Audio / streaming): Apple streaming protocol with multiroom synchronisation.
- Google Cast (Audio / streaming): Google streaming protocol for casting audio and video to devices.
- Spotify Connect (Audio / streaming): Streams Spotify directly to a device without routing through the phone.
- DLNA / UPnP (Audio / streaming): Discovery and streaming standard for sharing media on a local network.
- SunSpec Modbus (Solar / industrial): Standard register map that lets monitoring software read inverters and batteries across brands.
- OCPP (EV charging / protocol): Open Charge Point Protocol, the standard link between a charger and a charging network.
- Matter bridge (Interoperability): A device that exposes non-Matter products to a Matter fabric.
- Wi-Fi sensing (Sensing / RF): Using changes in Wi-Fi signal to detect motion or presence without a dedicated sensor.

## Cloud platforms covered

- AWS IoT Core (AWS): Strong ecosystem; store service status and region differences
- Azure IoT Hub / Azure IoT Edge (Microsoft Azure): Enterprise integration and device provisioning
- Oracle Cloud Infrastructure IoT (Oracle Cloud): Use official service status and regional availability
- Google Cloud Pub/Sub / Edge ecosystem (Google Cloud): IoT Core retired; position as migration and ecosystem page
- IBM Cloud IoT / Watson IoT history (IBM Cloud): Verify current service lifecycle before publishing
- Alibaba Cloud IoT Platform (Alibaba Cloud): Separate China and international regions
- Tencent Cloud IoT Hub (Tencent Cloud): Check international product availability
- Huawei Cloud IoTDA (Huawei Cloud): Focus on device access and regional availability
- Volcano Engine IoT / Edge (Volcano Engine / BytePlus): Volcano Engine serves China and Asia; BytePlus covers international markets. Verify product naming and regional availability.
- Droplets / App Platform (DigitalOcean): Server backend and hosting rather than IoT device platform
- Cloud Compute / Kubernetes (Vultr): Server backend and hosting
- Linode / Akamai Cloud (Akamai / Linode): Edge and hosting comparison
- Public Cloud / Bare Metal (OVHcloud): European data residency angle
- Cloud / Dedicated (Hetzner): Value pricing and EU residency
- Tuya IoT Platform (Tuya Cloud): Tie provider pages to device/brand pages
- EMQX Cloud / EMQX Enterprise (EMQX): Strong MQTT intent
- Particle IoT Platform (Particle): Bundle hardware, SIM and platform
- Ayla IoT Platform (Ayla Networks): Enterprise OEM platform
- Losant Enterprise IoT Platform (Losant): Workflow and edge angle
- Blynk IoT (Blynk): Low-code and maker audience
- PTC ThingWorx (ThingWorx): High-value B2B leads
- Siemens Insights Hub (Siemens Insights Hub): Industrial edge and digital twin
- SAP Edge Services / Business Technology Platform (SAP): Enterprise integration angle
- Ubidots (Ubidots): SMB and maker platform
- Datacake (Datacake): LoRaWAN and low-code
- Arduino Cloud (Arduino Cloud): Maker and education audience
- HiveMQ Cloud / Enterprise (HiveMQ): MQTT broker comparison
- Cloudflare Workers / R2 / Durable Objects (Cloudflare): Useful for site and IoT backend architecture
- Scaleway Instances / IoT Hub (Scaleway): European cloud and IoT hub angle

## Common questions

**What is IoT Atlas?** An independent IoT decision platform: a structured catalogue of devices, brands, protocols, companion apps and cloud platforms, with editorial comparisons and implementation guides.

**Is the marketplace ranking data real?** No. Amazon ASINs, ranks, prices and ratings on this site are placeholder sample data for layout review. They must be replaced with a licensed data source before they can be relied on.

**Are the brand scores a valuation?** No. The brand coverage index describes what a brand catalogue covers across ten dimensions. It is editorial opinion based on public information, it is not a rating or certification, and it is not a financial valuation or investment recommendation.

**How are comparison scores produced?** Each comparison scores both options 0-100 on named decision factors. The weighted total is the average across factors. Readers can re-weight the factors on the brand index to get their own ordering.

**What is verified in each app record?** The app name, its category and its store links. Many store links point to an official store search rather than a direct package listing; those are labelled store-search. An app is attributed to a parent company only when it is that vendor first-party app or the relationship is documented.

**Can a brand request a correction?** Yes. Brands and manufacturers may request a correction, clarification or removal using the corrections policy. Supported requests are applied and the change is noted.

**What is not medical advice?** Nothing here. Health and medical device listings are educational only and are not medical advice.

## Content rules

- Health and medical listings are not medical advice.
- Legal pages require jurisdiction-specific review before production.
- Community contributions are user-generated and carry their own disclaimers.
- Corrections policy: see https://hi-spark.net/corrections-policy.html
